Theme

Latin word

contrā

adverb

by contrast, on the other hand; in return; opposite, over against (especially across water); on the contrary, the other way; on the other hand, on the contrary

In this lexicon

  • contrast

    also used · classical · Pac. ap. Auct. Her. 2.36: sunt autem aliī philosophī, quī contrā Fortūnam negant ūllam exstāre (Lewis & Short)

  • in exchange for

    also used · classical · Catull. 13.9: sed contrā accipiēs merōs amōrēs

  • opposite

    also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 5.13: cujus ūnum latus est contrā Galliam (Lewis & Short s.v. contrā); Traupman 354

  • reverse

    also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.84 (Lewis & Short)

  • whereas

    also used · classical · Traupman 325

  • contrā + acc.: against

    classical

  • contrā animum: against my better judgment

    classical

  • contrā dīcō, contrā dīcere, contrā dīxī, contrā dictum: contradict

    classical

  • Aspicedum contrā mē.: look me in the eye

    classical

Examples

  • fortūnam īnsānam esse … perhibent philosophī … sunt autem aliī philosophī, quī contrā Fortūnam negant ūllam exstāre

    philosophers say that fortune is mad … but there are other philosophers who, by contrast, deny that there is any such thing as FortunePac. ap. Auct. Her. 2.36 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for contrast

  • sed contrā accipiēs merōs amōrēs

    but in return you will get pure loveCatull. 13.9

    In the entry for in exchange for

  • Immō contrā: ille mē pulsāvit, nōn ego illum.

    No, the other way round: he hit me, not I him.composed
